claims.text: The proposed framework separately calculates lattice and electronic thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice thermal conductivity can be calculated using machine-learned interatomic potentials and Green–Kubo molecular dynamics.
Electronic thermal conductivity can be calculated separately from DFT electronic states using Boltzmann transport theory.
The machine-learned force field accounts for variations in atomic masses, force constants, and defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
The framework captures the transport effects of approximately 1 wt.% oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr.
The integrated framework will be 20–30% more accurate than Debye-temperature or perfect-crystal approaches.
The relevant initial material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr with inherent atomic-scale disorder and minor oxygen contamination.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions of HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The model is applicable to bulk, defected HfNbTaTiZr up to 1200 K.
Atomic-scale disorder and point defects alter local interatomic force constants and mass distributions.
Disorder and point defects mediate distinct phonon- and electron-scattering mechanisms in HfNbTaTiZr.
Training machine-learning potentials on ab initio data captures the effects of disorder and defects on vibrational transport.
Separate Green–Kubo and electronic Boltzmann calculations prevent conflation of lattice and electronic heat-transport channels.
The framework accommodates temperature-dependent changes in phonon and electron scattering.
The predictions will reproduce a crossover below 200 K at which lattice and electronic contributions are nearly equal.
The predictions will maintain fidelity through 1200 K.
Earlier relevant models used elastic-property or Debye approximations for perfect, defect-free crystals and conflated or approximated lattice and electronic contributions.
The method may not apply directly to nanostructured samples or samples with severe extrinsic defects.
Accuracy outside 200–1200 K is unverified.
Electrical-conductivity measurements with Lorenz-number evaluation and vibrational measurements can provide independent estimates of electronic and lattice contributions for falsification.

contradictions.description: The model is asserted to cover temperatures below 200 K and to reproduce a sub-200 K crossover, while the boundary states that accuracy outside 200–1200 K is unverified.
